summary: Tenant residency stickiness resets after API key rotation causing intermittent cross-region routing and p95 latency spikes
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent routing of requests to US edges immediately after rotating their API key in the Console. Requests are intended to stay pinned to eu-west but ~30-50% briefly route to us-east for a short window after rotation. This introduces an extra TLS/egress cost and increases client-observed p95 from ~120ms to ~700–900ms for affected windows.
impact: Degraded chat UX for FinNova users during key rotation windows. Multiple tenants under the account experienced repeated p95 bursts during business hours. Business impact: higher perceived latency and potential SLA implications for enterprise tier.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Log into Console and perform API key rotation for a tenant pinned to eu-west.
2) Immediately issue generation calls with residency=eu-west and model gpt-4o-instruct.
3) Observe edge selection via SNI/TLS and measure client-side p95.
4) Repeat rotation via the public API with residency header included and compare behavior.
expected_behavior: After key rotation, residency binding remains intact; requests continue to be routed to eu-west edges with no significant p95 regression.
observed_behavior: Short-lived period (approx 10–30s) where a subset of requests select us-east edges despite residency header. Client-side p95 increases by ~600–800ms during this period. Control-plane audit logs show token-swap attempts without residency metadata.
logs: Edge trace ids: trace-7f3a2, trace-88b1c. Control-plane audit: api-key rotation event tn-2198 @ 2026-03-09T08:03:11Z. Auth logs: token-issue entries missing 'residency' claim for several rotations. Edge logs: SNI selected 'us-east.edge.redwood.ai' for requests that included residency header 'eu-west'.
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses:
- Token rotation path may emit a new token that lacks the residency-stamp claim for a short window, causing residency-mapper to fall back to nearest default edge.
- Cache invalidation race between auth service and residency-mapper: edges see the new token before control-plane metadata has propagated.
- Console UI rotation flow performs async metadata write after key activation in some code paths.
Checks performed:
- Reproduced in staging by rotating keys via Console; observed residency omission in ~12% of rotations.
- Correlated rotation timestamps with edge traces; timing matches the reported p95 spikes.
- Searched for similar tickets and found related routing race reports (see linked issues).
Preliminary conclusion: ordering bug in Console->auth->residency pipeline causes temporary loss of residency stamp during rotation, resulting in fallback routing and latency spikes.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Support (Aisha Patel): Customer submitted traces and timestamps; initial triage shows correlation with key rotation events. Requested control-plane and auth logs and asked SRE to reproduce in staging.

2026-03-11 - SRE (Marina Kovacs): Reproduced locally in staging using Console rotation. Observed token issuance without residency claim for ~18s before metadata propagation. Created PR to adjust ordering and added unit tests; PR linked above.

2026-03-12 - Customer (Emilia Duarte, FinNova): Tried rotation via API (including residency header) and saw no issue; asks for ETA for fix and whether the API approach is an acceptable interim workaround.
2026-03-12 - Support (Aisha Patel): Communicated workaround and ETA. Notified Product and Auth teams and scheduled a production canary window.
resolution: In progress. Fix merged to staging (PR 1452). Production hotfix scheduled for 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC with canary rollout. Workaround: use API rotation with explicit residency header or postpone Console rotations to off-peak windows.
next_steps: 1) Execute canary rollout and monitor client p95 for tenants performing rotations. 2) Backfill regression test to prevent residency-claim omission. 3) Update Console rotation flow to ensure residency metadata write completes before key activation. 4) Notify affected customers and document recommended rotation procedure.
